name: Morisyen

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Morisyen (mori1278).
French lexifier: Morisyen (Mauritian Creole) draws the large majority of its vocabulary from 18th-century colonial French. Baker & Kriegel, APiCS ch. 'Morisyen'; Corne (1999) From French to Creole.

Malagasy substrate: enslaved and indentured population brought from Madagascar contributed to the founder population of Isle de France/Mauritius alongside East African and Indian labourers (Baker & Kriegel, APiCS ch. 'Morisyen').
East African (Bantu, represented here by Swahili as the closest specced proxy) adstrate: enslaved population drawn from the East African coast during the French colonial period.

Bhojpuri adstrate: 19th-century indentured Indian labourers (mostly from the Bhojpuri-speaking Gangetic plain) form a large share of the modern Mauritian population and contribute an ongoing contact layer (Baker & Kriegel, APiCS ch. 'Morisyen').

notes: French-lexifier creole of Mauritius written in a Latin, largely phonemic orthography. Grapheme map follows the modern conventions: ou [u], ch [ʃ], j [ʒ], z [z], gn [ɲ], ng [ŋ]. NASAL VOWELS: a vowel spelled with a following <n> nasalises only when that <n> closes the syllable (word-final or before a consonant); before a vowel the <n> stays a plain onset consonant and the vowel stays oral (allophone_rules, not enumerated digraphs -- see docs/allophony.md). RHOTIC: <r> is an onset approximant [ɰ] but a coda <r> is silent, lengthening the preceding vowel instead (allophone_rules). Standardisation of the spelling is recent and older French-etymology spellings still circulate; the phonetic value of some contextual variation (loanwords, frozen French compounds such as 'bien') is not fully recoverable and any prosody is left unencoded, so a PER floor is expected.

allophone_rules.notes: Onset <r> (syllable-initial, before a vowel, incl. clusters like <gr>/<fr>) surfaces as the labio-velar approximant [ɰ], not the French uvular fricative (Baker & Kriegel, APiCS ch. 'Morisyen', on the Morisyen rhotic): frer [fɰɛː], gran [ɡɰɑ̃].
Coda <r> (before a consonant or word-finally) is not pronounced; its mora surfaces as compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (see MFE_LENGTHEN_*): ser [sɛː], larzan [lɑːzɑ̃].
Compensatory lengthening for a deleted coda <r> (Baker & Kriegel, APiCS ch. 'Morisyen'): ser [sɛː], pangar [pɑ̃ɡɑː].

A vowel before a coda nasal consonant nasalises and backs/lowers (Baker & Kriegel, APiCS ch. 'Morisyen', orthography section; Baker & Hookoomsing 1987 Diksyoner Morisyen): gran [ɡɰɑ̃], non [nɔ̃], morisien [moʁisjɛ̃], bezwin [bezwɛ̃]. The nasal letter itself is silent (see MFE_NASAL_ABSORB); a following-vowel context (fenomenal [fenomenal]) leaves the nasal an onset consonant and the vowel oral.
